sentences.text: It be checked and registered .

Present : Mr. Hitesh Pandey, Advocate with the petitioner.
 ORDER 1. Heard.
2.
The petitioner is sister-in-law (bhabhi) of the respondent No. 2 (nanad).

3. The petitioner filed criminal revision petition under Section 397 Cr.P.C. against order dated 28.09.2019 challenging discharge of the respondent No. 2.
4.

The trial Court discharged the respondent No. 2 on the ground that the allegations against the respondent No. 2 are vague and non-specific, as under:
"Perusal of the file further reveals that there are no specific allegation of dowry demand and entrusted of dowry articles against the accused Smt. Swati Kochar (sister-in-law) in the entire complaint.
No specific date and time has mentioned regarding the dowry demand made by them.
Further no specific role has been described.
In view thereof, the said accused Smt. Swati Kochar stands discharged for the punishable u/s 498A/406 IPC."
5. Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner contended that there are specific allegations against the respondent No. 2.
He contended that the petitioner has made date and month-wise allegations against the respondent No. 2.
He referred the complaint made by the petitioner in this regard.
6. Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner contended that the trial Court wrongly concluded that the allegations against the respondent No. 2 are vague and non-specific.
He contended that the respondent No. 2 has marital discord with her husband and she was residing in matrimonial house of the petitioner.

He contended that the judgment in Neera Singh vs. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) &
Ors., Crl. M.C. 7262 of 2006 decided on 23.02.2017 is not applicable to this case.

sentences.text: 7. The Court has examined the charge-sheet and particularly, complaint made and referred by the petitioner.

8. The petitioner stated, in para No. 18 of the complaint, that the respondent No. 2 returned to her (petitioner) matrimonial house and fought with her husband and occupied her room on 1 st floor of the house.
In para No. 19, the petitioner stated that she conveyed her problem to her husband but he told him that she had to sleep down stairs with his parents.

In para No. 20 and 21, the petitioner Richa Puri vs . State & Anr. on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89237111/
1 stated that she was not allowed to enter into her room and the respondent No. 2 was using her room and clothes.
She stated that they did not allow her to watch TV and use AC.
She stated that they used to force her to bring gift and ear-ring from her parents.
She has also made mention of an incident on the issue of use of shampoo in which the respondent No. 2 shouted at her for using her shampoo.

These are the allegations made by the petitioner against the respondent No. 2.
9.
On holistic reading of the allegations made by the petitioner against the respondent No. 2, this Court is of the considered opinion that the allegations are vague, non-specific and general in nature.
The trial Court did not commit any error in discharging the respondent No. 2.
Accordingly, the criminal revision petition filed by the petitioner is dismissed.
A copy of order be sent to the trial Court.
The criminal revision file be consigned to record room.
Digitally signed by SANJAY SANJAY SHARMA SHARMA
